Title: Cry for help as French-Swiss lake dries up
Article:
THE picturesque Lac des Brenets between France and Switzerland has dried up after a record-breaking hot summer, leaving locals crying out for help to save the lake.
Indeed, the words "HELP" and "SOS" have been scratched out in the weeds now flourishing on the exposed lake bed.
The drought has ruined pleasure boat tourism, while some question whether the lake will ever return to enduring full health.
"It's absolutely heartbreaking. It really is emotionally devastating, because it's utter despair: no more lake," said amateur local historian David Favre, who lives in the Swiss village of Les Brenets.
"As children, we used to spend all our summers swimming at the beach, having fun by the water, diving, jumping in and sometimes even fishing," the 76-year-old told AFP.
But "since the last drought in 2018, it's been a disaster. Unfortunately, the lake empties out every couple of years, or soon, perhaps every year," he added, saying he felt the authorities have "completely abandoned" the lake.
The Doubs river rises in the French Jura mountains and normally forms a lake at Les Brenets, where it begins to mark the border between France's Franche-Comte region and Switzerland's Neuchatel canton.
The lake ends at 27-metre-high waterfall, which has now stopped flowing.
The lake has dried up due to a combination of factors, including geological fissures that drain water underground, below-average rainfall and repeated heatwaves.
The months of June, July and August were each the hottest ever recorded in Switzerland since measurements began in 1864.
Every day Yvan Durig, owner and captain of the Lac des Brenets navigation company, measures the level of the remaining basin of water which is shrinking away at the very deepest bit of the lake.
"Normally, we have 25 or 30 metres of depth here," but now there are only nine metres of water left, and within it "the fish are really chock-a-block", he said.
[[nid:1547427]]
While locals are used to periods of low water, this particular spell is alarming, with the record low of 1906 set to be surpassed imminently.
A task force was set up by French and Swiss authorities in 2022, notably to explore ways of limiting the water draining into the fissures, but has not resulted in decisive action.
"We had to halt boat operations on July 20," said Durig.
"Just imagine: having to stop right in the middle of the season like that. It's unbearable for a company like ours," he said.
"Normally, these are times when we transport 200 to 300 people a day," said Durig.
Pontoons and dozens of boats lie stranded on the dry lake bed.
The water level monitoring station for the lake is now so far out of the remaining basin that Durig does the measurements manually.
The water line is dropping around 20 to 22 centimetres a day.
On October 1, it fell to an elevation of 735.34 metres above sea level – fully 14.66 metres below where it should be.
Within days, it is expected to surpass the 1906 record drop of 15.35 metres.
A tiny stream now trickles through the weeds on the lake bed.
Maxime Fallet, who works at a Doubs riverboat excursion company, fears the lake is "destined to disappear", for lack of a plan to save it.
"The atmosphere in Les Brenets these days, when talk turns to the Doubs, is often tinged with a certain sadness, a melancholy at the thought that we could lose this lake – a lake that has been part of the soul of Les Brenets for generations," he told AFP.
Durig feels time is running out.
"We must take action – indeed, be proactive – and seal the lakebed," he said.
"But this can no longer take years. That is simply not an option anymore."
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Brunei Sultan departs after witnessing F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP return to Sepang
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, departed for home today after concluding his special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
The aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, took off at 5.30 pm after a red carpet send-off, which included a guard of honour mounted by 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Malay Regiment.
Minister of Youth and Sports Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari, Brunei High Commissioner to Malaysia Dato Paduka Abdu’r Rahmani Basir and Chief of Protocol Ambassador Mohd Ikram Ibrahim were present at the Bunga Raya Complex here to bid farewell to His Majesty and his delegation.
Earlier, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah attended the F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at SIC with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei to witness the return of the prestigious F1 race to Sepang after a nine-year absence.
Also attending the race were Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
F1’s return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain’s King Hamad Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before being dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Boy mauled by pack of five stray dogs in Bachok receives rabies jab, shows signs of recovery
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 4 — An eight-year-old boy who was seriously injured after being attacked by a pack of stray dogs at Pantai Kuala Kemasin, Bachok, on Thursday has received a rabies vaccination and is now being monitored for three weeks.
The boy’s mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, showed positive progress today after remaining withdrawn for two days as he was still traumatised by the incident.
“For two days after the incident, he was still frightened and did not want to talk. He mostly kept to himself and sometimes cried because he was in pain from his injuries, especially to his head and neck.
“Thankfully, his condition has improved today and he has started talking. He can now answer when asked and can recount what happened during the incident,” she told reporters at Raja Perempuan Zainab II Hospital here today.
Earlier, Rosnani and her son were visited by the Kelantan Education Department (JPN) Student Development Sector deputy director, Norazan Mat Nor.
Recalling the incident, Rosnani said Azuar Firdaus was playing on the beach around 9.30 am with three relatives when five stray dogs approached.
She said the three relatives, aged between two and 11, managed to run away, but Azuar Firdaus fell while trying to escape and became the dogs’ target.
“He tried to escape by running into the sea, but the dogs continued chasing him until someone came to his aid and rescued him. He was semi-conscious after the incident and suffered injuries to his head, neck and hand, including bite wounds, in addition to scratches on his back,” she said.
Rosnani said her son underwent a five-hour surgery the day after the incident to treat his injuries.
She said Azuar Firdaus also received a rabies vaccination and is expected to continue being monitored for about three weeks.
Meanwhile, Norazan said the department is aware of the incident, which is believed to be the first involving a student being seriously injured in a stray dog attack.
He added that the victim has shown positive progress and is expected to be discharged from hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Amanah says Pakatan open to partners to form stable Melaka govt ahead of state election
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 4  — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to seeking allies to form a stable government in Melaka in the upcoming state election, said Amanah secretary-general Muhammad Faiz Fadzil.
He said Amanah’s stand was that it was better for the coalition to find partners who could work together to form a stable state government.
Muhammad Faiz said a decision on possible cooperation was expected to be made soon but the possibility of PH contesting on its own remained open.
“Amanah believes that joining forces with allies who want to establish a stable government in Melaka would be better,” he told reporters after the LKIM chairman’s engagement session with Telok Mas fishermen at the Tanjong Nibong fishermen’s jetty here today.
Muhammad Faiz said any decision on political cooperation would be determined by the PH Presidential Council, but Amanah had been exploring collaboration with various parties.
In the 2021 state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while PH took five and Perikatan Nasional two.
The Election Commission is meeting on Wednesday to set the dates for the state polls. — Bernama

Title: Fabricated aviation emergencies betray a global trust — Shahrul Mizan Ismail
Article:
OCTOBER 4 — In aviation, a lie can become an operational hazard. False information can alter a pilot's decisions, mobilise rescue services and trigger security responses with consequences for human life. Fabricating a crash or staging a hijacking therefore raises a question more serious than whether a stunt is offensive: has deception crossed the threshold into unlawful endangerment?
International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence. — AFP pic
International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence.
Article 1(1)(e) of the 1971 Montreal Convention directly addresses someone who unlawfully and intentionally communicates information they know to be false, thereby endangering an aircraft in flight. A crash is not required. Knowledge of falsity and the resulting danger to the aircraft are central.
[1]
The distinction matters. A fabricated bomb warning can have legal consequences even when the aircraft lands safely. Conversely, an honestly reported concern that proves unfounded is not automatically a deliberate falsehood. Passenger distress alone cannot substitute for evidence of the danger required by this provision.
Hijacking requires a separate analysis. Under the 1970 Hague Convention, the core offence involves someone aboard an aircraft in flight unlawfully seizing or exercising control through force, threats of force or intimidation. An imaginary bomb can therefore support a real hijacking if the threat achieves the unlawful seizure of control.
[2]
But a performance during which the pilot retains lawful control does not automatically establish that offence merely because passengers were deceived. Other offences may still arise. The 2010 Beijing Protocol broadens the framework, including technological means and specified threats made in circumstances indicating credibility. Treaty participation and the date of the conduct determine which framework applies.
[3]
False distress communications also deserve attention. Article 47 of the International Telecommunication Union Constitution requires member states to take steps to prevent false or deceptive distress, urgency, safety or identification signals. Radio Regulations provision 15.1 prohibits false or misleading transmissions. A fabricated crash report accompanied by a false distress signal may therefore engage obligations beyond the hijacking conventions.
[4]
State involvement makes the stakes greater. Article 4 of the Chicago Convention commits contracting states not to use civil aviation for purposes inconsistent with the convention's aims. Sovereignty over airspace carries responsibilities; it cannot itself legitimise manufacturing a threat for political advantage.
[5]
The diversion of Ryanair Flight FR4978 to Minsk on 23 May 2021 supplies a documented institutional example. ICAO Assembly Resolution A41-1 records the Council's determination that senior Belarusian government officials knowingly participated in, or were involved in, supplying information about a false bomb threat that led to the diversion.
[6]
The Assembly endorsed the determination that the government's actions deliberately endangered the aircraft and those aboard, amounting to a flagrant and serious violation of Article 4. This demonstrates the international consequences of a fabricated threat without a crash. It must, however, be distinguished from a criminal conviction of any particular individual.
State responsibility and individual criminal liability are separate questions. The International Law Commission's articles on state responsibility provide a framework for asking whether conduct is attributable to a state and breaches its international obligations. State organs, delegated governmental authority, instructions and control can be relevant. Political benefit alone does not prove attribution.
[7]
If an aviation incident is fabricated to blame another country and justify military action, the United Nations Charter's prohibition on the use of force also becomes relevant. Applying its principles, a state cannot manufacture a right of self-defence from an attack it knows never occurred. A false narrative cannot supply the missing factual basis.
[8]
During armed conflict, international humanitarian law distinguishes permissible ruses from perfidy. Article 37 of Additional Protocol I prohibits killing, injuring or capturing an adversary through betrayal of confidence in protection afforded by that law. Not every deception meets those requirements. Calling conduct a war crime requires proof of the relevant context and elements.
[9]
The practical response should combine institutional resolve with fair process. Investigators need preserved communications, crew testimony, flight data and a reconstruction of operational decisions. Alleged state involvement requires careful examination of instructions and institutional links. Authorities must establish jurisdiction and the applicable domestic implementing law, rather than assume that every treaty permits every country to prosecute every incident.
The same evidential discipline must govern accusations that a disaster was staged. Incomplete footage, early inconsistencies or unanswered questions do not themselves establish a conspiracy. Demanding a credible explanation is legitimate. Converting uncertainty into an unsupported allegation damages the very public trust that accountability is supposed to protect.
Aviation depends on people treating emergency information as a responsibility. Deliberately exploiting that trust warrants consequences where the legal elements are proved. International law earns its authority by protecting life firmly and assessing accusations fairly. The trust that allows humanity to cross the skies must never become a prop in somebody else's performance.
*This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

Title: Negeri Sembilan joins Johor on unhealthy air list as haze lingers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111).
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (151) and Seremban (146), while Samarahan, Sarawak, recorded a reading of 117.
Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and an API exceeding 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Another woman files report against motivational speaker as Perlis police probe alleged sexual harassment
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant.
“The case is being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act,” he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the man is currently under a two-day remand order ending today in connection with a police report lodged in Padang Besar.
He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.
He added that an application for remand to assist investigations into the Kangar case would be made at the Kangar Magistrates’ Court tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: F1 roars back at Sepang as Sultan Ibrahim, Bahrain and Brunei royals watch on
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.
His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15 pm by Bahrain Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35 pm.
The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; the Tunku Mahkota of Kedah, Tunku Shazuddin Ariff Sultan Sallehuddin; and the Tengku Mahkota of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; also attended the race, marking the return of the roar of F1 engines to Sepang after the last race was held there in 2017.
The race, scheduled to start at 3 pm, was slightly delayed due to heavy rain after Negaraku and the Bahrain national anthem were played.
The event is expected to attract nearly 100,000 spectators and will also feature a fly-past by Gulf Air aircraft before the race gets underway.
Cars enter the pit lane after the start of theGulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race was delayed by heavy rain at the Sepang International Circuit on October 4, 2026, which marks F1’s return to Malaysia after a nine-year absence. — AFP pic
Four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull Racing will start the 56-lap race from pole position, followed by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes-AMG Petronas.
In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.
F1’s return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama

Title: Motorcycle skids towards drain near Taiping, killing 76-year-old rider
Article:
IPOH, Oct 4 — An elderly man was killed and a woman who was the pillion rider was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding skidded at Lorong Kampung Boyan 1, Kampung Boyan near Taiping, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 76-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers.
He said they received a call about the incident at 12.41 pm before a fire engine from the Taiping Fire and Rescue Station arrived six minutes later.
“Upon arriving at the scene, personnel found that the Yamaha Ego motorcycle ridden by the two victims had skidded and nearly fallen into a drain in front of a house. The elderly man was unconscious while the 69-year-old woman suffered serious head injuries,” he said in a statement today.
Sabarodzi said firefighters lifted the male victim, who was nearly falling into the drain, before MOH medical officers confirmed his death.
“The injured victim was given initial treatment before being sent to the hospital, while the male victim’s body was handed over to the police for further action, and the operation ended at 1.49 pm,” he said. — Bernama

Title: After F1 and KL Marathon, October’s only getting busier with Melaka election dates on Wednesday and Budget Friday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — October has got off to a positive start for Malaysia, marked by a vibrant sporting calendar, strong performances by national athletes and encouraging developments in the economy and investment, while several major national agendas await as the month unfolds.
The first weekend of the month saw Malaysia become a focal point for sports fans as the roar of Formula 1 (F1) machinery once again echoed at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years, with Malaysia hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026.
The return of the prestigious race to Sepang, which last hosted an F1 event in 2017, coincided with two other major international sporting events, the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) 2026 and the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026.
The 30th edition of LTdL, which began on Sept 27, will conclude in Putrajaya today after eight stages across the peninsula, while KLSCM, held yesterday and today, saw more than 30,000 local and international participants take to the streets of the capital.
The sporting excitement at home was accompanied by strong performances by the national contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan, which had secured nine gold, seven silver and 16 bronze medals as of yesterday.
The haul included historic team gold medals for the men’s and women’s squash teams, a keirin gold for track cycling champion Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang, and the men’s sepak takraw squad’s first team regu gold in 36 years.
National sporting success also extended to the football pitch as Harimau Malaya ended their Fifa Asean Cup 2026 group-stage campaign with a 6-0 victory over Singapore.
Although the result was not enough to send the national squad into the final, the team is set to face Vietnam in the third-place playoff tomorrow.
The positive trend was also reflected in the economy, with the ringgit showing resilience in a challenging global environment, ending the first week of October trading at 4.0820/4.0870 against the US dollar.
Malaysia’s investment momentum also received a boost as the country and Singapore explored efforts to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
Companies from the republic have so far committed more than S$5.5 billion in investments in the zone, covering sectors including advanced manufacturing, data centres, energy technology and solar energy.
On the international front, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s involvement was also expanding through Petronas, which holds a 25 per cent stake in the C$33 billion (about RM94.7 billion) LNG Canada Phase 2 expansion project.
The project could open up further investment and business opportunities for Malaysian companies in Canada’s energy and infrastructure sectors.
Following Anwar’s meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Prince Salman Hamad Al Khalifa, yesterday, Malaysia also welcomed Bahraini investments in areas including Islamic finance, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing.
The two countries also encouraged Malaysian companies to use Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market.
Despite the positive developments at the start of October, Malaysia continues to grapple with transboundary haze, which has caused a decline in air quality in many areas nationwide.
Six areas recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels, while 37 were at moderate levels and only three recorded good readings.
As October progresses, attention will turn to several major agendas expected to shape the country’s economic and political landscape for the remainder of the year.
Most immediately, focus will be on the Dewan Rakyat sitting, which begins tomorrow, with the tabling of Budget 2027 by the Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, scheduled for Friday.
The budget will be among the country’s most closely watched economic agendas this year, with attention expected on measures to tackle the cost of living, raise incomes, stimulate growth and strengthen economic resilience amid a challenging global environment.
The Pre-Budget 2027 Statement had outlined 10 focus areas centred on the Madani Economy and 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) priorities, including tackling the cost of living, increasing incomes, creating quality jobs and strengthening the economy and governance.
Political activity is also expected to intensify this month as the 16th Melaka State Election (PRN) moves into the next phase following the dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly on Sept 23.
The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting this Wednesday to determine key dates for the election, including nomination and polling days, as negotiations and cooperation among political parties remain a focal point.
Senior Lecturer in Political Science at the Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Mujibu Abd Muis, described October as a crucial month that could determine the direction and pace of the country’s politics in the final months of 2026.
He said developments taking place almost simultaneously, including the Melaka state election, internal party dynamics and the tabling of Budget 2027, could shape public perceptions ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).
Mujibu viewed the Melaka state election not merely as a battleground to determine the state government, but as a potential ‘political laboratory’ for parties to test their respective strengths, strategies and cooperation formulas.
He said the election would follow two previous state polls involving Johor and Negeri Sembilan, while also providing political data that could influence seat negotiations, candidate selection and coalition alignments ahead of GE16.
Mujibu said Budget 2027 would serve as the most tangible test of the government’s economic credibility, noting that the public would evaluate it not merely based on figures but on the extent to which announced measures affect their lives, including disposable income, the cost of living, employment and economic opportunities.
“With two months remaining until the end of 2026, October provides an opportunity to assess the political landscape. Parties will look at the Melaka state election results, gauge the public’s response to the Budget, assess their respective organisational strengths and then begin making more serious calculations for GE16.
“In summary, October may not be the month that determines who will win the general election, but it could be the month that determines who starts to emerge as being in the lead, who is losing momentum and who needs to change their strategy,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Petros assurance rings hollow amid challenge to Petronas, says Zaid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim says Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurance that Petros will not undermine Petronas rings hollow while the state oil company seeks a bigger role in the gas business and Sarawak continues to question the federal legal framework governing petroleum.
Writing on Facebook, Zaid said the central issue was Petros’s desire to take over the gas aggregator role currently performed by Petronas in Sarawak.
That role is integral to the gas value chain, he said, and cannot be transferred without affecting Petronas’s commercial position. He estimated Petronas’s Sarawak gas business at about RM10 billion annually.
Zaid said the impact was already visible in the confusion created by competing claims over payments. He pointed to the Shell dispute, saying roughly RM80 million a month had been withheld while the parties disputed who should be paid.
Abang Johari had said earlier that Petros’s expansion was not designed to displace Petronas. He said Sarawak would continue to work with Petronas while developing its ability to process gas locally and move into higher-value downstream activities.
His comments followed Petros’s joint development agreement with Norwegian company Höegh Evi for a Kuching LNG regasification terminal, which is expected to be operational by 2029. Sarawak is also exploring small-scale LNG facilities and carbon capture, utilisation and storage projects.
Zaid said those ambitions need not be incompatible with Sarawak’s development, but the order of discussion mattered. The state must first recognise Petronas’s rights over Malaysia’s oil and gas under the Petroleum Development Act 1974, he said.
He noted that Sarawak was challenging the application of the PDA and other federal petroleum laws in the state. That, he said, was a challenge to the legal foundation of Petronas, rather than a routine negotiation over commercial participation.
Once the legal position is accepted, Zaid said, the parties can negotiate a role for Petros that addresses Sarawak’s circumstances without dismantling key functions of the national oil company.
He warned that the consequences would extend beyond Sarawak if other producing states pursued similar claims. Petronas would lose the scale that supports its national role, including its ability to invest and contribute to federal revenue, he said.

Title: JPJ hunts illegal motorcycle ride operators ferrying passengers to Sepang F1 circuit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is tracking down individuals and groups offering illegal motorcycle ride-hailing services to transport visitors and spectators attending the Formula One (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
According to
Berita Harian
, the operators were found advertising their services through various social media platforms, offering rides from several locations to the circuit grounds and between SIC and nearby parking areas.
A survey of social media postings showed that both car and motorcycle transport services were being promoted, although motorcycles appeared to be the preferred option among spectators seeking to avoid heavy traffic congestion around the circuit.
On Threads, some riders were offering trips between Mitsui Outlet Park Sepang and SIC for RM10 each way. Others advertised motorcycle taxi services, commonly referred to as “gojek”, charging RM10 for journeys between Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) and SIC.
The report also found touts offering rides for as much as RM80 for a 10-kilometre journey from Mitsui Outlet Park to a Petronas station near the main entrance of the circuit. Some operators were also said to provide helmets for passengers.
While the services have attracted visitors looking for a faster alternative to traffic-clogged roads, concerns have been raised over safety risks, particularly in the event of accidents or other unforeseen incidents.
JPJ is understood to be conducting an enforcement operation around SIC and several hotspot locations near the circuit and KLIA. Authorities are also taking action based on information and advertisements that have gone viral on social media.
The enforcement comes amid an influx of spectators attending the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix, with traffic congestion around the Sepang circuit area drawing widespread attention over the weekend.

Title: Government to follow legal process over Bandar Utama school stabbing suit
Article:
IPOH, Oct 4 — The government will allow due process to take its course following a civil suit filed by the family of a 16-year-old girl who was killed in a stabbing incident at a school in Bandar Utama last year, Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) M. Kulasegaran said today.
NST reported that Kulasegaran said he would not comment further on the legal action as the matter involved the Ministry of Education and he did not have full details of the case.
“I don’t want to jump the gun. The actions by the government and the police will follow the normal process unless something unusual happens,” he told reporters after launching the Madani Kita Programme with the Buntong Community 2026 at the Kampung Tersusun Multipurpose Hall in Buntong here.
The civil suit was filed at the Kuala Lumpur High Court on Oct 1 by the mother and sister of Yap Shing Xuen, who was killed in the incident. According to a statement by Yap’s mother, the suit names several government agencies, the parents of the boy responsible for the fatal attack, and the boy himself as defendants.
The family said they believed the teenager’s death could have been prevented had appropriate measures been taken, particularly in addressing mental health issues among students.
Asked whether existing laws should be strengthened to include mental health provisions, Kulasegaran said the government was not currently drafting any new legislation on the matter. Instead, discussions were ongoing with relevant agencies and non-governmental organisations.
He also stressed the importance of helping parents better understand their children’s needs, including mental health concerns. Kulasegaran said he had recently met more than 1,000 parents during a programme in Serdang aimed at equipping them with skills to better support their children.
“The programme is conducted over 10 weeks, with three-hour sessions every weekend, to guide parents in understanding the needs of their children,” he said.
Kulasegaran noted that approaches to disciplining children had evolved over time, adding that mental health issues should be addressed more proactively. He said support should be extended to those affected, noting that mental health challenges also impacted a segment of the civil service.
“Action should be taken to help them,” he said.

Title: Raincoat and umbrella check: Storm warning for KL, Putrajaya and six states until 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and six states until 4 pm today.
It said in a statement that the adverse weather was expected to affect Perak (Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah and Hilir Perak) and the whole of Selangor.
A similar warning was also issued for Kelantan (Pasir Puteh and Bachok) as well as Terengganu (Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus and Kuala Terengganu).
In Sarawak, the affected areas are Limbang (Limbang), Miri (Marudi), Sri Aman (Sri Aman and Lubok Antu), Betong (Betong), Bintulu (Tatau), Sibu (Selangau) and Kapit (Song).
As for Sabah, the areas involved are the Interior (Pensiangan, Sipitang, Tenom and Tambunan), Tawau (Kalabakan and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan) and the West Coast. — Bernama

Title: Rapid KL adds eight more shuttle buses as MRT Putrajaya Line repair work continues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Repair works are underway to restore power supply and train services on the Putrajaya Line following a cable theft near the Taman Equine MRT Station, according to Rapid KL.
It said alternative train services and free shuttle buses remained available to help passengers get to their destinations during the disruption.
“Alternative train services and free shuttle buses are still operating to assist passengers, with eight additional buses deployed to facilitate passenger movement,” it said in a statement.
The service disruption was caused by a loss of power following a cable theft near Taman Equine Station, which was detected at 5.24 am today.
Following the incident, a train was stranded at the station, while technical teams were mobilised to inspect the affected area and carry out the necessary repair works to restore power supply and train services.
Rapid KL also advised passengers travelling to Sepang via the ERL from Putrajaya Sentral to use alternative routes via the KL Sentral or Bandar Tasik Selatan ERL stations.
Station staff and auxiliary police personnel have also been deployed at stations and bus stops to help manage passenger movement.
Rapid KL said it would provide updates on the service status from time to time through its official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: Water in the tank at Batu Kawan? Penang team looks into viral claims of vehicle trouble after refuelling
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 4 — The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) in Penang is investigating claims that several vehicles experienced problems after refuelling at petrol stations near Batu Kawan.
A Penang KPDN spokesperson said the ministry was aware of the claims and had sent a team to investigate.
“The Penang KPDN has taken note of the claims of vehicles experiencing problems after refuelling at a petrol station near Batu Kawan.
“We will send a team to look into the matter and issue a media statement afterwards,” the spokesperson said in a statement today.
Earlier, several posts went viral on social media alleging that vehicles experienced problems, including being unable to start, after refuelling at several petrol stations around Penang.
The posts also claimed that the problem was suspected to have been caused by water-contaminated fuel, but this has yet to be confirmed by the authorities. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials KPDN in Malay stands for Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup.

Title: Brother under seven-day police remand after Terengganu man’s death
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Oct 4 — A man suspected of murdering his elder brother in Kampung Banggol Tasek, Bukit Payong, Marang yesterday has been remanded for seven days from today until Oct 10.
The remand order for the 42-year-old suspect, a person with a mental disability, was issued by Kuala Terengganu Court Assistant Registrar Yuhanis Mohd Roslan at Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) today to facilitate further investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
In the incident at about 9 am yesterday, a 43-year-old man died after allegedly being struck with a blunt object.
The victim’s 36-year-old sister was also injured and is warded at HSNZ after she allegedly tried to prevent the suspect from attacking the victim.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said today that dissatisfaction with his elder brother, who allegedly frequently asked their parents for money, is believed to have led to the fatal attack. — Bernama

Title: Consulate: Malaysians must enter Southern Thailand legally if they plan to get married there
Article:
SONGKHLA, Oct 4 —Malaysians planning to get married in southern Thailand have been reminded to enter the country through legal routes and with valid travel documents to ensure that a confirmation letter can be issued by the Consulate General of Malaysia in Songklha.
Malaysia’s Consul General in Songkhla, Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi, said that if they entered the country illegally, such as through unauthorised routes, the consulate would not be able to issue the confirmation letter due to violations of Thai immigration laws.
He added that the consulate’s confirmation letter was important for court procedures related to the registration of the marriage in Malaysia.
“Not many, but there are still (Malaysian couples), as some come to us to request confirmation, but we cannot give it because, in principle, when they enter Thailand and commit an immigration offence, it becomes difficult for the consulate to issue the confirmation.
“We need to respect the laws of Thailand, so I urge Malaysians to understand this,” he said during a visit by a delegation from the Perlis Journalists Association (PWP) to his office at the Consulate General of Malaysia in Songkhla here on Friday (Oct 2).
Meanwhile, Ahmad Fahmi said that, so far, about 70 Malaysians are being held in prisons in southern Thailand, with the highest number in Narathiwat.
He added that the majority of them were being held in connection with drug-related cases. — Bernama

Title: Fadhlina vows full review after student’s death in Yong Peng, says MOE will cooperate with police probe
Article:
YONG PENG, Oct 4 — Education Minister Datum Seri Fadhlina Sidek today said the Ministry of Education (MOE) will conduct a thorough review of all matters under its purview following the death of a student in Yong Peng, Johor, while police continue their murder investigation.
In a Facebook post, Fadhlina said she travelled to Yong Peng this morning to personally obtain updates on the incident and received briefings from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Johor Education Department (JPN), the Batu Pahat District Education Office (PPD), and the school involved regarding the chronology of events and actions taken so far.
She also met the victim's family at Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail in Batu Pahat, expressing condolences and stressing that the family deserved answers regarding the tragedy.
According to information provided by police, the victim was found unconscious within the school compound and was later pronounced dead. A 16-year-old male teenager has been detained and remanded for six days to assist investigations. The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, while the motive and cause of the incident remain under investigation.
Fadhlina said she had instructed that all matters under the ministry's responsibility be scrutinised, including student attendance records for supplementary classes, school security controls, and patrol procedures. She added that the school's security company had also been asked to cooperate with the review.
“If there is any negligence or responsibilities that were not carried out as they should have been, firm action will be taken,” she said.
The minister said MOE would give its full cooperation to police and would not pre-empt the ongoing investigation. Counselling support is also being provided to affected students and school staff.
She urged the public to respect the investigation process and give the victim's family space, saying the truth should be established based on facts rather than speculation.

Title: Missing 77-year-old found dead after car plunges into Sungai Petani river
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 4 — The body of an elderly man who went missing after the vehicle he was driving skidded off the road and fell into a river at Jalan Lubuk Segintah-Lubuk Kawah here was found at 9.15am today.
Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the body of Mat Yusof Hashim, 77, was found between 50 and 100 metres from where his vehicle was located in the river.
“The victim was fully clothed when found. His body was sent to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Setar for a post-mortem,” he said in a statement today.
Earlier, it was reported that the victim’s vehicle had been recovered from the river, but no body was found after it was pulled ashore.
Hanyan also thanked members of the public, particularly the owner of a video showing the incident, for promptly alerting police. — Bernama

Title: Money row emerges as suspected motive in Terengganu man’s death, brother under remand
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 4 — Dissatisfaction with his elder brother, who allegedly frequently asked their parents for money, is believed to have led a mentally challenged man to attack and beat his brother to death in Bukit Payong here yesterday, police said.
Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said police received information about a fight at a family home in Kampung Banggol Tasekat at about 10.55am.
He said initial investigations found that the 43-year-old victim, the suspect’s elder brother, died after being allegedly beaten with a blunt object, while the suspect’s 36-year-old sister was also injured when she tried to stop the attack.
“The 42-year-old suspect, who is a person with a mental disability, was arrested by police by the roadside in Bandar Bukit Payong shortly after the incident.
“He was believed to be dissatisfied with his brother, who has a drug-related record and allegedly frequently asked the family for money,” he told a press conference at the Terengganu police contingent headquarters here today.
He said the suspect’s sister was receiving treatment at Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital after suffering a wound to the back of her head, a fractured right thumb and a minor injury to her spleen.
Mohd Khairi said the suspect was remanded today to facilitate investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder. — Bernama

Title: From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst.
Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement.
“Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today.
Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement.
Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia.
He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa.
Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend.
Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement.
“Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said.
Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit.
He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending.
“Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit. Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said.
Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports.
RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said.
Mohd Mizan also said that access to the World Cup through legitimate and accessible channels represented a form of social inclusion, as major sporting events could create shared experiences cutting across race, age, geography and income.
“Few things temporarily dissolve Malaysia’s normal social divisions as effectively as sport. During major football tournaments, mamak restaurants, living rooms, community halls and public viewing areas become shared national spaces,” he said.
He said Anwar’s approach showed that diplomacy today operated far beyond formal conference rooms, with Malaysia using F1 and Fifa to bring the world closer to its people while strengthening its position on the global sporting stage.
“Sometimes diplomacy happens through bilateral negotiations. Sometimes it happens through football and sometimes, at 300 kilometres per hour around Sepang,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar orders ‘immediate, thorough and transparent’ probe into Yong Peng student’s death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed his condolences over the death of secondary student Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairoul Faisal, whose body was found with injuries at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, yesterday.
In a Facebook post, the prime minister extended his condolences to the family of the Form Four student and prayed that they would be given strength and fortitude in facing the difficult ordeal.
Anwar also directed the authorities to conduct an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation to determine the cause and establish what actually happened.
“If there are elements of a crime, firm action must be taken in accordance with the law,” he said in the post.
Anwar said the safety of children was a shared responsibility and that the government would not compromise on ensuring their safety and wellbeing.
In the incident at about 5.30pm yesterday, Irene Sofiya, 16, was found dead with injuries on her body, believed to have been murdered in a secondary school hall in Yong Peng.
The victim was found by her grandmother and a friend who went to the school after she failed to return home despite her extra classes having ended. — Bernama

Title: Johor exco tells Education Dept to cooperate fully with investigators after Yong Peng student’s death
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 4 — The Johor State Education Department (JPNJ) has been told to extend full cooperation to assist investigations into the death of a Form Four female student at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, yesterday.
State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said JPNJ and the District Education Office should also provide the necessary support to the victim’s family and the affected school community.
He said the state government viewed the incident seriously, especially as it involved the safety and welfare of students within the school area.
“I wish to emphasise that there will be no compromise on any form of bullying, violence or criminal acts that threaten the safety of the school community.
“… however, whether this incident involves such elements must be determined based on the outcome of official investigations rather than speculation,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Dr Muhammad Naqib said schools must remain safe places to pursue their education, build their future and be in an environment that safeguards their safety and well-being.
He also conveyed his condolences to the victim’s family over the heartbreaking tragedy and expressed hope that they would be given strength and resilience in facing this difficult time.
According to media reports, a Form Four female student was found dead, believed to have been murdered, at a secondary school in Yong Peng, near here, yesterday.
Police, however, have yet to issue any official statement regarding the incident. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: JPNJ is the Malay abbreviation of Jabatan Pendidikan Negeri Johor.

Title: Cable theft disrupts MRT Putrajaya Line, with longer waits at UPM, 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Train services on the MRT Putrajaya Line are experiencing delays following a power supply disruption caused by a cable theft incident near Taman Equine Station, according to Rapid KL.
In a statement, Rapid KL said the incident was detected at 5.24 am today when a train was unable to move at Taman Equine Station, prompting its technical team to conduct inspections and repair work to restore the power supply and train services.
Following the disruption, passengers are expected to experience longer waiting times on platforms, particularly at UPM, 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral stations.
To assist passengers in continuing their journeys, alternative train and shuttle bus services have been activated, involving trains from Kwasa Damansara Station turning back at UPM Station at 10-minute intervals, as well as trains operating between UPM and 16 Sierra stations, also at 10-minute intervals.
Shuttle trains between 16 Sierra and Putrajaya Sentral stations are operating at seven-minute intervals, the statement said.
In addition, free shuttle buses are operating between Serdang Jaya, UPM, Taman Equine, Putra Permai, 16 Sierra, Cyberjaya Utara, Cyberjaya City Centre and Putrajaya Sentral stations at intervals of 15 to 20 minutes, depending on current traffic conditions.
Passengers using the Putrajaya Line to travel to Sepang via the ERL service at Putrajaya Sentral are advised to allow for longer travel times due to the disruption.
Rapid KL also advised passengers to use alternative routes via KL Sentral and Bandar Tasik Selatan ERL stations.
“To ensure the safety and smooth movement of passengers, auxiliary police personnel and station staff have been stationed on platforms and in station concourses to assist passengers. Regular announcements on train schedules are also being made at the stations,” it said.
Rapid KL takes the cable theft incident seriously as it could affect the smooth operation of services and operational safety.
It will continue to monitor the situation and provide the latest updates on service status from time to time via its social media platforms and journey-planning app. — Bernama

Title: Murdered schoolgirl was well-liked, good student, says friend
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — A Form Four student found dead in a secondary school in Yong Peng yesterday was among the school's top academic performers and had been expected to achieve straight As in her Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination next year, according to a classmate.
The friend said the 16-year-old victim's absence during an extra class session had initially raised little concern among classmates, who assumed she was unwell.
A teacher had asked about the student's whereabouts during the lesson, but none of the pupils knew why she was absent, the classmate said.
“I only later learned that she had not returned home. At the time, I never imagined that anything serious had happened to her,” the student said.
The friend recalled that a teacher contacted students after sunset to ask about the timing of the additional classes, prompting suspicions that something was wrong.
“When I asked the teacher why, I was eventually told that something bad had happened at the school. I was shocked and never expected such an incident could occur,” the student said.
Describing the victim, the friend said she was highly focused on her studies and actively involved in school activities. Her academic record had led many to believe she was capable of obtaining straight As in next year's national examination.
“She was dedicated to her studies and active in school programmes. That is why we still cannot believe what has happened. We can still picture her face and never thought we would lose her,” the friend said.
The girl was found dead at about 5.30pm on Thursday inside the school's hall, with injuries on her body. Police are treating the case as a murder.
She was discovered by her grandmother and a friend who went to the school after becoming concerned when she failed to return home following the end of extra classes.
According to the report, the victim had been living with her grandmother after her mother died of cancer several years ago, while her father works in Kuala Lumpur.
The victim was reportedly found with dried blood on her body and bruises consistent with an assault. A broken flower pot was also found near the scene.

Title: Lahad Datu deputy police chief Jimmy Panyau dies at 53 after liver-related complications
Article:
LAHAD DATU, Oct 4 — Lahad Datu deputy police chief Supt Jimmy Panyau died last night at the Kuching Life Care Society in Sarawak after suffering from liver-related complications.
Lahad Datu police chief ACP Dzulbaharin Ismail, when contacted, confirmed the death and said Jimmy, 53, died at 9.30pm.
“He was a dedicated officer throughout his service in Lahad Datu,” he said.
Dzulbaharin said the Iban officer had sought treatment at Borneo Medical Centre in Kuching on Aug 14 after experiencing liver-related health problems.
“He was subsequently admitted for further examination and treatment before being discharged on Aug 15 and given medical leave until Aug 23,” he said.
Dzulbaharin said Jimmy had also undergone a medical examination at Gleneagles Hospital, Kota Kinabalu, where a growth was detected in the liver and bile duct area.
“On Aug 20, he sought treatment at Sarawak General Hospital before being admitted to the Male Surgical Ward for further monitoring and treatment,” he said.
Jimmy had previously served as Mukah police chief in Sarawak. — Bernama

Title: Not a great day to be outdoors in Batu Pahat, Segamat and Kluang as API hits unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Six areas in Johor and one in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9am today.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) of the Department of Environment, Batu Pahat recorded the highest reading at 156, followed by Segamat (154), Kluang and Tangkak (152), Larkin (148) and Pasir Gudang (126).
In Sarawak, Samarahan recorded a reading of 152.
Fifty-seven areas recorded moderate API readings, while three areas were at good levels, namely Sandakan (45), Langkawi (37) and Kangar (32).
The API reading for the Kota Kinabalu station was unavailable at that time.
API readings of zero to 50 are categorised as good, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and above 300 (hazardous). — Bernama

Title: Final-year student falls for RM100-a-day ‘accounting job’ that turned her bank account into a mule account
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 4 — A final-year business student here, aged 22, has become the latest victim of a mule account scheme.
Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) Public Complaints Bureau chief Milton Foo said the case began on Sept 20 when the student was searching for online jobs via Facebook.
She later found the job offer, after which she was contacted by an individual via WhatsApp and was offered a part-time online accounting job, with payment of RM100 a day.
“However, the task was to receive money from certain individuals through her bank account,” said Foo at a press conference held at SUPP headquarters here.
On Sept 22 and 23, a sum of RM12,246 was deposited into her bank account from five individuals, and after that, the fund was transferred to two other accounts.
Following that, a sum of RM20,117 was deposited into her e-wallet account from eight individuals, before being transferred to six different accounts as per instructed.
“However, the victim did not receive the promised pay, and that the suspect disappeared and could no longer be contacted.
“She later found out that she was being used by the suspect after noticing that her bank account had been frozen.
“Checks done by her on the Semak Mule portal showed that there were three police reports lodged on her bank account: each in Sentul, Sri Petaling and Kelana Jaya.
“She then lodged a police report on Sept 29,” said Foo.
The SUPP man stressed that this incident served as a reminder to university students and fresh graduates to not be easily deceived by job offers obtained from social media.
“A job offer asking the job-seekers to use their own bank accounts to receive and transfer money is a definite red flag,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Three male students detained over murder of schoolgirl Irene Sofiya
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Oct 4 — Police have detained three 16-year-old male students in connection with the alleged murder of a Form Four student whose body was discovered at a school in Yong Peng yesterday.
According to
Berita Harian
, the suspects were arrested several hours after the body of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, was found at about 5.30pm.
Sources said one of the students is expected to be brought before the Batu Pahat Magistrate's Court this morning for a remand order to allow police to continue their investigation.
All three suspects are believed to be students at the same school attended by the victim. Authorities suspect Irene was brutally killed before her body was abandoned inside the school's hall.
The victim was reportedly found by her grandmother and a friend who had gone to the school looking for her after she failed to return home.
Police have not yet released further details on the motive or circumstances surrounding the case, and investigations are ongoing.

Title: Keling and Kumang the cows? Dayak group demands answers from Sarawak Agrofest organisers
Article:
MIRI, Oct 4 — Dayak Native Initiative (Dani) has criticised the use of the names Keling and Kumang for two cattle featured at the Sarawak Agrofest, saying the choice was insensitive to Iban customs and heritage.
In a statement, Dani said images of information boards identifying the cattle by the names had been circulating online, prompting concern among members of the Iban community.
The group said Keling and Kumang were highly respected figures in Iban folklore and tradition, with the names carrying deep cultural and spiritual significance for many Iban people.
“Using them for livestock at an exhibition has offended our community, whether it was done deliberately or through a lack of understanding,” it said.
Dani called on the Sarawak Agrofest organisers and those responsible for the display to explain publicly how the names were selected and approved.
It also urged the organisers to change the names immediately if the information boards remained on display and issue an apology to the Iban community.
The group further called on event organisers to consult Iban community leaders and the Council for Native Customs and Traditions when using names or symbols with cultural significance at public events.
“Names and symbols that hold deep meaning for a community should be carefully reviewed before they are used at public events,” it said.
Dani also urged the relevant customary authorities to examine whether the incident constituted a breach of adat and, if so, determine the appropriate course of action through the proper channels.
It stressed that any finding of a breach or imposition of customary sanctions should be made by the authority with jurisdiction.
Dani said Sarawak was a shared home for many communities and that respect for different cultures should be reflected in actions, including matters that might otherwise be regarded as minor.
“Respect Iban culture. Uphold the dignity of every community in Sarawak,” it said. — The Borneo Post
